extracted.intended_audience: professional and aspiring photographers, imaging professionals, and people interested in photography industry advocacy
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, best practices, and advocacy positions relevant to professional photographers and imaging professionals (business procedures, copyright practices, technical reproduction, and digital preservation). Useful for photographers seeking guidance on contracts, rights, and technical workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Business Practices in Photography
rubrics_metrics.description: A compilation of recommended procedures, industry terminology, and standard forms and contracts (often informally referred to as the 'Business Bible').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published and regularly revised by ASMP (seventh edition released 2008); aimed at photographers to provide recommended procedures, standard forms and contracts, and industry terminology for running a photography business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright registration and rights management (tutorials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Web tutorial on registering copyrights and related guidance to help photographers secure legal rights in their images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASMP provides freely available material (e.g., tutorials) on registering copyrights; historically has lobbied for provisions granting copyright automatically to creators and supported copyright term extensions (life+50, later life+70).

rubrics_metrics.name: Model releases and property releases (forms and guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance and tutorials on using model releases and property releases to clear rights for published images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASMP offers information on model and property releases to help photographers create legally sound releases and understand when releases are required for publication or licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard forms and contract practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of standardized contracts and forms for licensing, assignments, and business transactions to protect photographers' interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included within ASMP's Professional Business Practices resource; encourages use of industry-standard language and procedures to address credit lines, unauthorized reproduction, payment terms, and scope of use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical recommendations for accurate digital image reproduction (UPDIG)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of technical recommendations for accurate reproduction of digital images developed by the UPDIG coalition (ASMP a founding member).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides technical standards and recommendations to ensure faithful reproduction of images across workflows and devices; intended to guide photographers and image users on color, metadata, and reproduction practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practices and tutorials for preserving digital images (dpBestflow)
rubrics_metrics.description: Published best practices and tutorials for digital image preservation developed/sponsored by ASMP (dpBestflow project, 2008–2011).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance on digital workflows, archival formats, metadata, and preservation strategies — produced with support from the Library of Congress to aid long-term stewardship of digital photographic assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocacy positions on copyright policy and orphan works
rubrics_metrics.description: ASMP's policy positions and advocacy to protect photographers' legal rights, including support for automatic copyright to creators, extension of copyright term, and mitigation of harms from orphan works proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASMP testifies before Congress, files amicus briefs, and participates in litigation to influence copyright law and policy; examples include support for provisions of the Copyright Act of 1976, the Sonny Bono Copyright Extension Act, and engagement on orphan works debates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional networking and specialty group participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation in local chapters, specialty groups, lectures, Brain Trusts, and online forums to share business/technical knowledge and support professional development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASMP maintains 37 chapters and specialty groups; recommends use of bulletin boards, listservs, social networks, and local meetings to facilitate information sharing, mentoring, and discussion of business-related questions.
